comment: Which of vercel/next.js's own e2e tests the compatibility harness runs against cdk-nextjs.
Passed to the harness as NEXT_EXTERNAL_TESTS_FILTERS (see .github/workflows/e2e-harness.yml) and
read by next.js's test/get-test-filter.js: `rules.include`/`rules.exclude` are minimatch globs over
test file paths, and `suites[file].failed` lists individual test-case names to skip within a file
`rules.include` is deliberately an explicit list rather than next.js's own
`test/e2e/**/*.test.{t,j}s{,x}`: every file still costs a `next build` of its fixture plus a deploy.
Those deploys are cheap but not free - all files share one stack (`hrns-shared`), created once by
scripts/e2e-warm.sh and then updated per file with `cdk deploy --hotswap-fallback`, which is ~1-2
minutes rather than the ~4 a fresh CloudFront distribution takes. Files run serialized (`-c 1`) for
that reason. The full tree would still be a thousand-plus builds, so widen this list as the adapter
Every file listed here has been run against a real deployment and observed to pass. Add nothing on
the assumption that it will - the first version of this list was three files, all of which turned
out to be unbuildable by cdk-nextjs (see `excluded-notes`). Any case cdk-nextjs fails for its own
reasons is a bug to fix, not a `failed` entry - if one has to be excluded anyway, say why in
docs/harness-coverage.md is the human-readable companion to this file: every screened file, its
outcome, and for each failure an explanation plus a verdict on whether it is a bug or acceptable.

edge runtime, generally: cdk-nextjs refuses at build time to deploy any output whose runtime is not `nodejs`
(`assertNodeRuntimes` in src/adapter/build-outputs.ts). That is a deliberate product limitation -
the edge runtime is deprecated in Next.js, and cdk-nextjs supports Next.js 16's Node-runtime
The check throws during `next build`, so a fixture containing *any* edge route or legacy
middleware fails wholesale and per-case `failed` entries cannot rescue it. Such files have to be
left out of `rules.include` entirely. ~522 of next.js's e2e files are edge-free, so this is not
much of a constraint on widening the list.
test/e2e/app-dir/app-static/app-static.t: Excluded: ~10 `*-edge` routes declare `export const runtime = 'edge'`. See the note above.
Worth revisiting as a source of individual cases to port, since it is the densest coverage of the
ISR/caching behavior cdk-nextjs's cache handler implements.
test/e2e/app-dir/actions/app-action.test: Excluded: the fixture ships a legacy edge `middleware.js`. See the note above.
Excluded: the fixture ships a legacy edge `middleware.js`. See the note above.
test/e2e/app-dir/segment-cache/deploymen: Excluded pending investigation, NOT because the test is inapplicable - this one looks like a real
cdk-nextjs bug and should come back as a regression test once fixed.
`header with deployment id > header is set on RSC responses` fetches `<route>?_rsc=` with an
`RSC: 1` request header and expects `content-type: text/x-component`. Through cdk-nextjs it gets
`text/html; charset=utf-8`, i.e. the HTML render rather than the flight response. Failed all three
attempts, so it is not flaky.
Not the CloudFront header-quota caveat: `rsc` is in the dynamic cache policy's allowlist
(src/nextjs-distribution.ts). Whether the RSC request is being lost at the edge or mishandled by
the adapter's request bridge is not yet established.
revalidation behind the CDN, two files: Excluded as timing-inherent, not as a cdk-nextjs defect:
Each loads a prerendered page, calls a route handler that runs `revalidatePath`/`revalidateTag`,
asserts the handler returned `revalidated: true` (it does), refreshes immediately and expects new
content. The refresh is served from the CloudFront edge: a prerendered app-router page comes back
with `cache-control: s-maxage=31536000` and the second request to it reports `x-cache: Hit from
cloudfront` (verified by hand against a harness deployment).
cdk-nextjs does invalidate the edge on explicit revalidation (`invalidateCloudFrontPaths` in
src/adapter/s3-cache-handler.ts, and see docs/caching-guide.md), but fire-and-forget:
`CreateInvalidation` has no bounded completion SLA and these tests re-request within about a second.
Vercel purges its own CDN as part of the revalidate, which is why the tests are not gated out of

page instead of the prerendered route.
Untested hypothesis, from reading rather than measuring: src/runtime/lambda.mts deliberately hands
the runtime the raw percent-encoded path, and src/runtime/dispatch.ts looks the resolved pathname up
in `manifest.entrypoints` with a plain property access. If the manifest's keys are decoded and the
request's is not, nothing matches and the miss falls through to the static 404 - which is what a
404 with no error in the function logs looks like. Note that
segment-cache/encoded-slash-params (`%2F`) passes, so whatever this is is narrower than "encoded
test/e2e/app-dir/segment-cache/cached-na: Excluded pending investigation: 4 of 14 cases fail, the same 4 on every attempt. Three are the
`... from the initial HTML for subsequent navigations` cases, which fail with `Received a response
with an error status code` on a prefetch the client issues off the inlined app shell; the fourth
expects a fully static second navigation to issue no network requests at all and sees one.
The other 10 pass, including the equivalents that prefetch from a navigation rather than from the
initial HTML, so this is specific to the HTML-inlined prefetch path.

asserts a measured duration is `< 1500` and gets `NaN`, i.e. the navigation timing it wanted to
measure never happened. Timing-sensitive, and it was not flaky - it failed all three attempts.
test/e2e/app-dir/segment-cache/refresh/s: Not excluded by us, and there is nothing to run: the file is `describe.skip` upstream, commented
`Disabled because too flaky`. Recorded so it is not re-screened - it reports "passing" in about 5
test/e2e/app-dir/segment-cache/cdn-cache: Not excluded by us: next.js itself skips this file under `isNextDeploy`. Listed only as a worked
example of the README's claim that deploy mode gates out what cannot work behind a CDN.
test/e2e/app-dir/app-basepath/index.test: Excluded: 3 of 13 cases fail, all of them an action that calls `redirect()` (relative, absolute,
and to a path outside the `basePath`). The browser never leaves `/base/client`. The other 10 pass.
Deterministic - failed all three attempts of the 2026-09-22 run.
Not the `x-amz-content-sha256` bug that used to make every action POST 403 here (fixed; see
docs/harness-coverage.md). With that fixed the POST reaches Next.js, but the browser records no
response at all, and by hand the reply comes back `200 application/octet-stream` with no Next.js
headers and an HTTP/2 stream that does not close cleanly - the signature of a RESPONSE_STREAM
invocation whose `HttpResponseStream.from` prelude was never written. Under investigation; this is
a cdk-nextjs bug, not a `failed` entry.
